(a) Snapshot: at mint time, `linkedSnapshot: Array<{_id, uid, provider}>` of the CURRENT identities goes into OAuthState (intent 'link' only).
(b) After a `redeemed` result: re-read via listLinkedIdentities({db: state.invite.db, token: result.token}, state.linkPersonId, fetch). The just-bound identity = the entry whose _id is NOT in the snapshot. If its uid+provider pair matches a snapshot entry → DUPLICATE: DELETE property/<new _id> with result.token, then report profile_link_noop_same_identity (neutral style). If the DELETE returns non-2xx → console.warn with the status and continue to the same noop message (never fail the sign-in). If no snapshot pair matches → existing success path, unchanged. If no new entry can be identified → existing success path (do not invent an error).

(d) List de-dup: render one row per distinct uid+provider (first occurrence in entity order wins).

tasks.commitBody:
Profile link picker no longer blocks a provider that already has a
linked identity: all provider buttons stay enabled once the linked
list has loaded (linkedLoadFailed still gates the picker). The linked
identities list above the selector is de-duplicated by uid+provider.

The same-identity guard moves from a pre-mint refusal to the link
callback: the mint-time snapshot of linked identities rides the OAuth
state blob; after a redeemed exchange the callback re-reads the
identities on the invite db with the redeemed token, and if the newly
bound entry duplicates a snapshot pair it deletes the newer entu_user
property value and reports profile_link_noop_same_identity in the
neutral success style. A rights-refused delete is logged and never
fails the sign-in. Path C sequence and the conditional setToken that
preserves the user's other collectives are unchanged.

New key profile_link_noop_same_identity in en/et/lv/uk (en/et copy
from Gama's ruling on the issue).

Live gate (Mihkel): link a second Google account on an already-Google
person; both sign-ins work. Record the observed status of a
rights-refused property DELETE on the issue.

Closes #219
